Structural Relations Estimated After the Measurement Models

Source: R/sem_sam.R
sem_sam.Rd

Fits local structural-after-measurement (SAM) models using lavaan::sam(). Each measurement block is estimated separately, and the structural relations use a covariance matrix corrected for measurement error. Two-step standard errors account for estimating the measurement parameters. This offers an alternative to treating estimated factor scores as perfectly measured observations. A latent SEM remains available when this wrapper's narrower scope does not fit the study.

Usage

sem_sam(
  model,
  data,
  estimator = "ML",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  gamma_unbiased = TRUE
)

Arguments

model

A single-group lavaan model string with at least two simple-structure factors, at least three distinct continuous indicators per factor, and structural regressions among those factors. Indicators cannot cross-load. Derived parameters, explicit equality constraints, observed covariates, residual covariances, feedback paths, and latent interactions are outside this interface's validated scope.

data

Raw numeric observations on the model's indicators. Incomplete observations are refused; the function never drops cases automatically. Use a joint latent SEM with FIML for incomplete data. An indicator of model that data lacks is refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid (see dmar_metadata), as are columns of data that share a name.

estimator

"ML" (default) with normal-theory "twostep" errors, or "MLR" with "twostep.robust" errors. Both use local ML mapping and the ML measurement estimators; the covariance assumptions for inference differ. Numerical optimization versus an analytic solution does not determine which SE is appropriate.

conf_level

Confidence level, default 0.95.

gamma_unbiased

Logical, default TRUE. For robust inference, use lavaan's finite-sample unbiased moment-covariance correction. FALSE uses the empirical moment covariance (HC0 convention).

Value

A dmar_tbl with parameter labels, estimate, se, statistic, p_value, confidence limits, conf_level, and stage. Attributes retain the fit, requested and actual method, and the covariance limitation. tidy() retains the rows and glance() gives the method and sample size.

Details

This interface currently supports unweighted, single-level, complete continuous data. It verifies the actual local mapping and two-step SE method after fitting and refuses a substitution. These restrictions distinguish numerical agreement with independent complete-data oracles from evidence for other models or missing-data uncertainty calculations. Small or moderate samples can benefit from separating measurement and structural estimation (Rosseel & Loh, 2024), but SAM does not repair a misspecified or unidentified measurement model.

Returned intervals concern individual, original-unit parameters. The underlying fit's joint covariance matrix does not populate every cross-stage covariance. Consequently this function refuses user-defined parameters and does not report standardized structural intervals or intervals for effects combining measurement and structural estimates. The attached fit is retained for inspection with that limitation, not as a complete covariance matrix for arbitrary delta-method calculations.

References

Rosseel, Y., & Loh, W. W. (2024). A structural after measurement (SAM) approach to structural equation modeling. Psychological Methods, 29(3), 561–588. doi:10.1037/met0000503

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

model <- "visual =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t4_lozenges
          verbal =~ t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence + t9_word_meaning
          verbal ~ visual"
sem_sam(model, holzinger_swineford)
